planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into average to saline-alkaline soil in full sun; Willow Baccharis colonizes washes and floodplain swales, tolerating periodic flooding and salty ground.

directions: Plant in full sun in average to saline-alkaline soil; Willow Baccharis is a deciduous shrub reaching 3-9 feet, colonizing washes, floodplain swales, and overflow channels along the Rio Grande and its Trans-Pecos tributaries. Small tan-white flower clusters appear from May through July, followed by plumed seed heads typical of the genus. It tolerates saline and alkaline floodplain soils better than many desert shrubs, making it a useful choice for a difficult wet-dry cycling site.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into sharply drained limestone or gypsum soil in full sun; Candelilla forms dense clumps of leafless, waxy stems, the source of its historic wax-harvesting use.

directions: Plant in full sun in sharply drained limestone or gypsum soil; Candelilla is a leafless, pencil-stemmed, blue-green succulent forming dense clumps to 2-3 feet, growing on bare caliche and limestone slopes across the Trans-Pecos and Chihuahuan Desert, famously forming the 'candelilla ridges' of Big Bend. Small whitish flowers appear among the stems, which historically were harvested for their protective wax coating used in candle and cosmetic production. It thrives on the barest, most mineral soil, needing essentially no irrigation once established.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into sharply drained, mineral soil in full sun; Turk's Head Cactus is a solitary barrel cactus with hooked spines, found on limestone and caliche slopes.

directions: Plant in full sun in sharply drained, mineral soil; Turk's Head Cactus is a solitary barrel cactus to 12-20 inches tall, armed with distinctive hooked spines ranging from maroon to cream, native to limestone and caliche upland slopes of the Trans-Pecos. Large yellow flowers with a reddish throat appear in summer, followed by edible fruit. It is a genuine barrel-cactus specialist for a Chihuahuan Desert rock garden, needing essentially no supplemental water once established.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into well-drained desert soil in full sun; Allthorn forms dense, impenetrable spiny thickets and needs careful siting away from foot traffic.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained desert soil; Allthorn is a dense, leafless, green-stemmed, intensely spiny shrub reaching 6-10 feet, forming impenetrable thickets on Chihuahuan Desert basin flats and floodplain margins across the Trans-Pecos. Tiny white flowers give way to small black berries valued by wildlife. Its aggressive spininess makes it an effective living barrier or wildlife thicket, but it should be sited well away from paths or play areas given how dense and sharp the mature growth becomes.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring into well-drained limestone soil in full sun; Sandpaper Bush grows naturally on canyon rims and rimrock, a distinct niche from gypsum flats and riparian bosque already covered.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained limestone soil; Sandpaper Bush is an upright evergreen shrub reaching 3-6 feet with neat, rough-textured leaves that feel like fine sandpaper, native to limestone rimrock and canyon rims of the Trans-Pecos and Chihuahuan Desert. Nectar-rich white flowers appear from spring through summer, drawing a variety of pollinators to this otherwise understated shrub. It fills a limestone-canyon-rim niche distinct from the gypsum-flat and riparian-bosque habitats already represented in Chihuahuan Desert plantings.
